title: Lesson 20. Events — part 1
description: click, input, mouseover/mouseout, classList, e.target and a live profile card

learn.intro: Hi! Today our site starts **listening to a person** for the first time: clicks, typing, hovering the mouse. Let's go!

slides.text: Before, our site only showed things. Today it starts **listening to a person**: a click, typing, hovering the mouse — all of these are **events**.
The formula: `element.addEventListener("event", function)`. **What** we listen to, **which** event and **what** to do.
A click counter: every press adds 1. `let`, because the number changes.

The event name is **lowercase and without on**: `"click"`, not `"Click"` or `"onClick"`. And we pass the function **without brackets**: `changeText`, not `changeText()` — otherwise it runs right away on load.

check.prompt: The code `btn.addEventListener("Click", f)` works on a click.
check.explain: The event name is lowercase: "click". With a capital letter nothing happens.

check.prompt: Why is the counter declared with let, not const?
options: Its value changes on every click
const is not allowed in JS
check.explain: const can't be reassigned, and count = count + 1 changes the value.

slides.text: We build a «Subscribe» button like on YouTube: press it — it turns grey «Subscribed», press again — it comes back.
`classList.toggle("class")` — no class, it adds it; there is one, it removes it. `classList.contains("class")` answers `true` or `false`: is the class there now.
We change the button color **with a CSS class**, and JS only toggles the class. The subscriber count lives in a variable, so it resets when the page reloads.

check.prompt: What does btn.classList.contains("subscribed") return if there is no class?
check.explain: contains answers «is the class there?» — true or false.

check.prompt: classList.toggle removes the class if it is already there.
check.explain: toggle is a switch: missing — adds, present — removes.

slides.text: The `input` event fires **on every letter** in a field. The field text is in `input.value`.
You type a name — it appears on the page right away:
`name.length` — how many letters. You can show a «7 / 20» counter and turn it red when there are more than 15. And `maxlength="20"` in HTML won't let you type more.
Want to react to every letter — listen to `input`, not `click`.

check.prompt: Where is the text the student typed in the field?
check.explain: An input field's text is in the value property.

slides.text: `mouseover` — the cursor **entered** the element, `mouseout` — it **left**. Hover the smiley — it smiles 😃, move away — 😐 again.
CSS `:hover` can enlarge or recolor, but it **can't change the content** — the text or the smiley. You need JS for that.

check.prompt: Match the event and when it fires
pairs: A letter was typed in a field

slides.text: The handler function gets an **event object** — it is called `e` or `event`. It holds a lot, but for now we need one thing: `e.target` — **the element that was clicked**.
The color buttons recolor the whole page. The listener is the same, but the result differs — because `e.target` points to the pressed button each time.
Forget `e` in the function brackets — you get the error `e is not defined`. Write `function (e) { … }`.

check.explain: target is the «target»: the element the event happened on.

check.prompt: If you don't write e in the function brackets and then use e.target, you get the error e is not defined.
check.explain: The event object must be taken as a parameter: function (e) { … }.

slides.text: We put it all into a **live profile card**: type a name — it appears on the card, and the first letter goes in the round avatar. Press a color — the border and avatar change. The subscribe button toggles.

`name[0]` is the first letter of a string (indexes start at zero, as in arrays). `toUpperCase()` makes it a capital: «aziz» → «A». If the field is empty, there is no `name[0]` — so we check with `if` first.
Homework: a like button like on Instagram. 🤍 0 → press → ❤️ 1 and it turns red → press again → 🤍 0. The color — through a CSS class, not through style in JS.
Today your site started listening to a person for the first time.

check.explain: [0] takes the first letter, toUpperCase makes it a capital.

questions.prompt: An event is a user action the site can react to: a click, typing, hovering.
questions.explain: Everything a person does on the page is an event, and addEventListener listens to them.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks: call a function when the button is clicked
questions.explain: The formula: element.addEventListener("event", function). The event name is lowercase, without on.

options: The function runs right away on load, not on a click
All correct, it runs on a click
questions.explain: With brackets changeText() the function is called at once. Pass changeText without brackets.

questions.prompt: What is on the page after three clicks?
Fill in the blanks: toggle the class and check if it is there
questions.explain: toggle switches the class, contains answers true/false — is it there.

questions.prompt: The subscriber count in a variable stays even if you reload the page.
questions.explain: Variables live while the page is open. After a reload the script starts over.

questions.prompt: Which event fires on every typed letter?
questions.explain: input catches every change of the field — every letter.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks: show the length of the name from the field
questions.explain: The field text is input.value, the number of letters is .length.

questions.prompt: Match what you need and how to write it
CSS :hover can swap the smiley 😐 for 😃 on hover.
questions.explain: :hover changes the style (size, color), not the content. Only JS can swap the smiley: mouseover / mouseout.

questions.prompt: Why does the same handler paint the page in different colors?
options: e.target is the pressed button each time
The color is fixed in CSS
questions.explain: The color comes from the pressed button's text: e.target.textContent.

questions.prompt: Build a handler that receives the event object
questions.explain: We take the event object as the parameter (e), and e.target is the clicked element.

questions.prompt: Why the if (name === "") check in the profile card?
options: An empty string has no name[0] — we show «?» and «Your name»
questions.explain: If the field is empty there is no first letter and nothing to call toUpperCase() on.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks: the first letter of the name as a capital
questions.explain: Indexes start at zero: name[0] is the first letter. toUpperCase() makes it a capital.
